title: Phosphate–albumin coupling gives no clear incremental digit-symbol prediction across separately sampled NHANES cycles
abstract: A fixed serum phosphate-by-albumin interaction was tested beyond flexible individual laboratory measures, conventional mineral summaries and demographic covariates. Models were fitted in1173 NHANES2011–2012 adults aged60+ and tested without refitting in1384 independently sampled2013–2014 adults. Weighted DSST MSE increased from163.0692 to163.2028 points²; baseline-minus-augmented error was−0.1336 (conditional target-PSU95% interval−0.2986 to+0.0286; joint coefficient-refit interval−7.9199 to+8.4141). Sensitivity directions varied with regularization and weighting; source cross-validation did not favor augmentation. This does not demonstrate incremental predictive value, equivalence, causality or clinical utility. It does not rule out other representations or meaningful gains under better-identified models.
